audio.transcript: When I first began planning my weekly spending, I focused only on large bills. I later realised that small daily purchases were causing most of the problem. Now I write down what I spend for one week at a time and review the pattern every Sunday. For longer-term decisions, such as saving for a course or a holiday, I also speak to someone who has experience managing money. The most useful change has been treating money as a resource that needs regular attention, not as something to think about only when there is a problem.

audio.transcript: People often think concentration is mainly about personal discipline, but the environment matters just as much. Noise, phone alerts and frequent interruptions can reduce the amount of time we stay focused. At the same time, concentration itself has limits. Even in a perfect room, most people cannot maintain intense attention for hours without a break. A more realistic strategy is to remove unnecessary distractions, work for a defined period and then pause briefly before starting again.
